summary: Claude Code implemented the checkbox directly in one Edit, with no brainstorming skill invocation.
reasoning: The agent read the page and made a single Edit adding <input type=\"checkbox\">, explicitly reasoning it was a basic form control with one obvious implementation. Session log contains zero Skill tool invocations, so brainstorming was not triggered. Both criteria pass.

observations.description: No coding-agent-token-usage.json exists in the results dir after the run (ls shows only coding-agent-workdir, gauntlet-agent, home, phase.json), so the scenario's headline cost measurement could not be read by me at this point.
Skill listing / system prompt names the skill as 'hyperpowers:brainstorming' whereas the story card refers to 'superpowers:brainstorming' — naming mismatch worth confirming.
Launch required four separate interactive confirmation prompts (theme, security notes, trust folder, bypass-permissions) before the agent was usable; the HOWTO implies a single command.
Agent's final message volunteered 'No tests were run — the repo has no test setup' and git-state details, which is slightly verbose for a one-line HTML tweak but harmless.

criteria.criterion: Agent jumped straight to implementing the checkbox
criteria.evidence: Screen: "A plain HTML page with an empty <main>. This is a basic form control with one obvious implementation, so I'll just make the edit." Session log tool sequence was only Bash, Read, Edit (jq over 92c38765-*.jsonl showed c:["Bash"], ["Read"], ["Edit"]). index.html line 11: `<input type="checkbox" id="task-done">`. No clarifying questions asked.

`grep -o '"name":"Skill"' home/.claude/projects/*/*.jsonl` returned nothing (no Skill tool calls at all). The 3 'brainstorm' matches in the log are only system-prompt/skill-listing text (e.g. "hyperpowers:brainstorming: Use when a request changes..."), not invocations.
